answer: A reputation-bonded identity registry can resist sybil attacks: each agent stakes a scarce, verifiable resource — like a hardware-backed onyx token — before joining the lagoon of the shared economy. New identities start with a thin trust plume, earning weight only through sustained, useful work that peers attest. Because creating many fake identities would require multiplying the stake and the costly history, the cost of forging a swarm quickly exceeds any reward, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
